paragraphs: By way of introduction, my name is Joshua Chappell. My intent is to apply for the HVAC Service Technician position at [Company]. I am making a career change into the skilled trades, and I want to be straight with you about where I stand.

I do not have three years of HVAC experience. What I have is seven years of running my own field service business, and the habits that came with it. I scheduled my own jobs, drove to the site, handled the customer at the door, and finished the work. I held 5.0-star reviews for over an entire year and delivered 98% of my projects on time. I have spent years working on construction, trades, and industrial job sites, so ladders, attics, rooftops, and hauling 50 to 75 pounds of gear are normal parts of my day. I stewarded a $30,000 equipment inventory as a teacher and kept $1 million of technical equipment running in the field at Grand Canyon Education. I also spent two years teaching 90+ students a year on technical equipment, which is the same patience your posting asks for when assisting other technicians. I learn technical systems fast, I show up, and I would come in ready to work and earn the certifications this trade requires.
I appreciate that you value getting the job done right the first time and creating positive experiences for customers; these are all values that I strive to emulate.
Thank you for taking the time out of your busy day to read my letter. I look forward to the opportunity of doing an interview with you.
